clue.text: Discuss Dickens? Here he is!

definitions.note: an exclamation greeting someone who turns up just as they are mentioned

parts.note: to discuss something is to talk about it, to mention it
'the dickens' is an old euphemism for Satan, as in 'what the dickens?'

explanation.surface: A literature fan proposes a talk on Charles Dickens, and the novelist himself appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens' looks like the novelist, but here it is the mild oath 'the dickens', meaning the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when a person arrives at the very moment they are being talked about.

clue.text: Send me instant letter, suffering in Coventry?

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters of the words before it are put through torment and twisted

explanation.surface: Someone shunned by their friends begs for an urgent message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges the letters of ME INSTANT LETTER. 'Send' just links. To 'send someone to Coventry' is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in Coventry means being ostracised, with nobody speaking to you: a deliberate shunning by silence.

clue.text: For a purpose, set aside weapon in Oriental rescue-vessel

parts.note: Oriental means eastern, abbreviated E
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: Someone stashes a gun aboard an Eastern lifeboat for some secret reason.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to reserve or allocate them for a particular use.

clue.text: Over time, Pisa's tower will help jog the memory

definitions.meaning: the famous tower goes on leaning, so it will continue to be at an angle or tilt (a ship's 'list') as the years pass
jotting down items on paper aids recall later

explanation.surface: Over the years Pisa's leaning tower will remind visitors of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' is to continue; 'a list' is a lean, as a ship lists, which is what the Pisa tower does.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing down tasks or items on paper is a standard memory aid; the tower, meanwhile, goes on leaning.

clue.text: Woman found initially on religious island

indicators.note: initially picks out just the opening letter of the word found

parts.note: Iona, in the Scottish Hebrides, is where St Columba founded his monastery

explanation.surface: A woman is discovered on a holy island.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, common in Scotland, so a female person.

clue.text: The high numbers reforming apartheid

indicators.note: reforming means the word apartheid is formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Political figures rise as South Africa's apartheid system is reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: The chart of best-selling records, whose top songs are the most successful numbers.

clue.text: They're said as prosecutor goes round Number One Court

indicators.note: goes round says the prosecutor's letters surround the others

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, the American public prosecutor
I is the Roman numeral one, and also the speaker's own self

explanation.surface: A prosecutor walks around the principal courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicta are pronouncements or remarks, plural things that are uttered.

clue.text: Country means to transport a tenor between universities

parts.note: a van is a vehicle for carrying goods

indicators.note: between puts A and the tenor inside the pair of universities

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university, so two of them give two U's
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A country finds a way to move a singer from one campus to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanuatu is an island nation in the South Pacific.

clue.text: They all do arrangements with lovely, if wild, flower

indicators.note: to do arrangements with letters is to reorder them, as a florist arranges blooms

explanation.surface: Florists all make bouquets with a lovely bloom, if it is wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do arrangements with' rearranges THEY ALL plus LOVELY IF.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland plant with small fragrant white bells, found growing naturally in Britain.

clue.text: Maybe Sydney opener's gutted, caught by devious leg-trap?

indicators.note: caught by means held inside the rearranged letters
devious means winding or crooked, so leg-trap is bent into a new order
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the first and last letters of opener

explanation.surface: A cricket opening batsman at the Sydney ground falls to a crafty leg-side field trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' and 'gutted' both look like reactions to a dismissal, but they are signals. A leg trap is a cricket fielding plan and the opener is the batter who goes in first.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney is an example of a big harbour city, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: American always getting in the groove

indicators.note: getting in suggests going inside the words American always, where the answer sits spanning the two

explanation.surface: A Yank who is forever finding the rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' marks a hidden word across the two clue words. 'In the groove' looks like a set phrase, but 'the groove' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a channel or duct, such as an anatomical passage or a cut furrow.

clue.text: Falls, not for the first time turning over the Gunners

indicators.note: turning over says the word for repeated is read backwards

parts.note: something done not for the first time is done once more
the Royal Artillery, the Gunners, is RA

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles yet again while turning over the Arsenal football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Gunners' tempts as Arsenal FC's nickname, but here it is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Indian anti-drinkers hard to take blame over

indicators.note: to take means the letters for the abstainers and hard hold the blame inside

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members abstain from drink
to take the rap is to take the blame
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A Native American teetotal group finds it hard to accept blame.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains, an Indian in the old sense.

clue.text: Consider getting put in report?

definitions.meaning: to consider is to allow for or weigh up
being written into a record or narrative, an account

explanation.surface: Should one think about being named in the official report?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: to put something into an account, a written report.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider a factor is to allow for it when judging; literally, a report is an account.

clue.text: Not clever enough to take pressure, my aims are food and lodgings

definitions.text: my aims are food and lodgings

indicators.note: to take means the words for stupid hold the pressure letter inside

parts.note: too thick means too stupid
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A dim lodger who can't take stress says all they want is bed and board.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the item speaks, and its targets are bits of food lodged between teeth, not meals and rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stick for removing scraps of a meal stuck between teeth, so its targets are those stuck bits.

clue.text: Bird depositing rubbish on island

parts.note: chaff is husks separated from grain, so worthless stuff
inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: A bird drops litter onto an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depositing ... on' just places the rubbish before the island in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European finch with a pinkish breast.

clue.text: Many elements so entitle coverage to be broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread about anew

explanation.surface: Broadcasting rights entitle a station to coverage of many events.
explanation.definitionFit: Elements such as fluorine and oxygen attract electrons strongly in bonds; many elements are described this way.

clue.text: The manufacture of cream

parts.note: the cream is the best people, the elite, so producing such a select group is the idea read cryptically

explanation.surface: A dairy process for producing cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream means the select few; a belief in favouring a select few creates that upper tier.

clue.text: Fearful time to go blundering

indicators.note: to go means the time letter departs from the words for frightened

parts.note: someone fearful is frightened, gripped by fright

explanation.surface: A frightened person makes mistakes when it is time to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To be blundering is to be mistaken, making errors.

clue.text: Motorbike victory?

explanation.definitionFit: A British motorcycle make and a word for a great win.

clue.text: Area between roads in Florida?

indicators.note: between puts the area letter inside the pair of roads

parts.note: M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI, so two roads give MI twice

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a patch of land between two highways in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; it is written MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on Florida's southeast coast, a place found in that state.

clue.text: Silk returning full-bodied cheese

indicators.note: returning says the word for plump is read backwards

parts.note: full-bodied means plump or fat
feta is a Greek white cheese

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a rich cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp fabric, traditionally woven from silk.

clue.text: This cat's no fool, getting a raise

indicators.note: getting a raise suggests lifting the letters upward, so in a down light they are read from bottom to top

parts.note: git is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A clever cat is rewarded with a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting a raise' reads NO GIT upwards in this down answer. 'Git' is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is a hybrid offspring of a male tiger and a lioness, so a big feline.

clue.text: Female clerical collars

indicators.note: collars means grabs hold of, so the clue word holds the name within it

explanation.surface: A woman in a clerical role wears dog collars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collars' looks like the noun of a priest's dog collar, but it is a verb: 'clerical' holds the name inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a girl's name, so a female.

clue.text: Where soldiers are trained to place their trust, for the most part?

definitions.text: Where soldiers are trained to place their trust
definitions.meaning: troops are drilled to rely on their commanding officer

explanation.surface: Most soldiers are trained to trust their commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, faith placed in a senior army officer; as an idiom it means usually or on the whole.

clue.text: Every — well, three man Jack?

parts.note: the idiom 'every man Jack' means everybody; a parallel idiom of ordinary men's names, three of them, completes 'Every' to mean the same

explanation.surface: Everyone, or rather three men, turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'every man Jack' and the three-name phrase after 'Every' mean absolutely everybody, any ordinary person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase lists three common male names standing for anyone at all, like every man Jack.
